text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] az1a - NIC TX jitter and host-level packet drops detected. Affected: inference-gpu-pool-1. Severity: P1. Pager oncall: @alice. (alert: https://alerts.redwood.example/1768809999)

alice: I'm looking. p50 token latency jumped ~3x, some streaming requests hitting 502 / connection reset.

sam: seeing increased retransmits on instance metrics, kernels showing tx-queue full on g5 instances. quick checks: `ssh host-az1a-123` logs show kernel tx_slow, dmesg snippet:
```
[ 1234.567890] net: tx-queue full, dropping...
```

alice: thanks. Ops, should we shift traffic to eu2 and usw2? We have spare capacity there.

ops-lead: yes. plan: 1) reduce DNS TTL to 30 2) enable region-fallback policy for inference-route 3) start target drain on az1a NLB 4) request temporary Dedicated nodes in eu2. I'll coordinate.

eng-ivy: small mitigation: enable prefix KV cache short-circuit to reduce cross-AZ fetches, and fallback to quantized model variant `gpt-small-q4` for latency-sensitive customers.

sean: kicking off `infractl reroute --from az1a --to eu2 --weight 70` now. watching route controller logs.

alice: started draining targets: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=i-0abc` (iterating). will post when 50% drained.

incident-bot: [ACTION] dnsctl set-ttl inference.redwood.example 30 (initiated by ops-lead)

sam: noticed ephemeral IP reassigns during drain; some pods re-initing, increased churn. added backpressure on autoscaler to avoid flapping.

ops-lead: Dedicated spin-up request submitted to capacity team, ETA first nodes ~8m. also prepping customer comms.

alice: customer-impact: retries from ~14 tenants, majority EU, a few NA sessions falling back -> higher latency. Customer-ops notified top 5 SLA accounts. Drafting status update now.

eng-ivy: applied service toggle: `--fallback-variant=gpt-small-q4` to route `low-latency`. small model keeps quality mostly intact but reduces token compute.

sean: reroute reported: `ok: 70% traffic to eu2, 30% to az1a`. p50 for routed requests down to baseline for the 70% slice.

alice: 50% of targets drained. NLB healthy host count decreasing. Keep monitoring connections (graceful drain window 300s).

ops-lead: if no improvement in 15m, we'll failover 100% and open a support case with AWS for ENI/host problem.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] incident assigned to oncall alice, severity bumped to P0 (potential SLA breach) at 1768810200

alice: all-hands: I'm taking pager, sam on infra, eng-ivy on model fallbacks, sean on routing. ops-lead handling customer comms.

sam: kernel team points to a possible NIC driver regression in the recent AMI rollout. pulling AMI rollout logs now.

alice: initiating full failover: `infractl reroute --from az1a --to eu2 --weight 100`

sean: 100% reroute applied, az1a traffic -> 0%. latency normalized across the fleet. beginning post-mortem capture.

ops-lead: AWS case opened for ENI jitter, ticket #123456. attaching logs + timeline.

alice: will prepare incident summary for customers and internal PM: include rollback AMI, tighter healthchecks, cross-AZ buffer, and routing automation.

incident-bot: [RESOLVE] incident resolved at 1768811400. Closure: move to postmortem channel and tag owners.

alice: thanks team. I'll run the postmortem template and assign action items.

sam: I'll block the AMI rollout until review complete. :thumbsup:

eng-ivy: I'll add an automated fallback rule to reduce impact for the next jitter spik e.

sean: adding reroute automation to trigger when tx-jitter > 25% for 2m.

ops-lead: consolidating notes, will schedule a follow-up with AWS. Good work everyone.
